metadata.case_name: CHAN KWAI NGOR v. LEUNG FAT HANG AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: a cleaner working in the Buddhist Hospital
plaintiff.occupation_after: working in a similar job as before (cleaner/amah at hospitals)

injuries.description: X-rays showed a compression fracture of the 12th thoracic vertebra.
source: X-rays showed a compression fracture of the 12th thoracic vertebra.

injuries.description: found the Plaintiff to have suffered from a minor crash fracture in the twelve dorsal vertebra (D12) with evidence of damage to D9, 10 and 11.
source: found the Plaintiff to have suffered from a minor crash fracture in the twelve dorsal vertebra (D12) with evidence of damage to D9, 10 and 11.

injuries.description: possible damage in the soft tissues such as cartilage and ligaments.
injuries.body_part: soft tissues (cartilage and ligaments) of the thoraco-lumbar region
source: there was possible damage in the soft tissues such as cartilage and ligaments.

manifestations.description: the Plaintiff was admitted to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital with a low back pain.
Physical examination revealed a weakness of her right leg and impaired sensation at the lateral aspect of her right thigh.
She complained of nagging back pain if she stands or sits for more than half to one hour.
She could not walk for more than half an hour without having to take a rest.
She also complained of numbness of the left leg.
There was only a reduction of 10° in the left leg on a straight leg raising test, being associated with pain.
No muscle wasting and reflexes were normal.

losses.description: Pain, suffering and loss of amenities (award under this head $80,000).
